chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from al-Sabbah ibn Sayaba, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who has difficulty in (reciting) the Quran will have two rewards, and the one who has ease in it will be with the former ones.'

key_terms.أَجْرَانِ: Two rewards — double recompense for difficulty and perseverance
key_terms.الْأَوَّلِينَ: The former ones — the pious predecessors, Companions, or those known for Quran mastery
key_terms.شُدِّدَ عَلَيْهِ: Had difficulty imposed on him — refers to the struggle of learning or reciting the Quran with effort
key_terms.يُسِّرَ عَلَيْهِ: Had ease granted to him — refers to fluent, effortless recitation

ai.seo_question: What reward does a Muslim get for struggling to recite the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that struggling with Quran recitation does not diminish one's merit — rather, it earns double the reward. This narration was addressed to early Shia Muslims who may have felt inadequate about their recitation skills compared to those who recited with fluency. 'The former ones' (al-awwalun) likely refers to the Companions of the Prophet and the pious predecessors who were known for their mastery of Quran recitation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Al Sabbah Bin Sayaba who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who has difficulty upon him regarding the Quran would have two Recompenses for him, and the one who has ease upon him, would be with the former ones’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mansur ibn Yunus from al-Sabbah ibn Sayabah who has said the following: “
I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘One for whom memorizing the Holy Quran is difficult, his reward is twofold and those for whom it is easy, they are with the pioneers (the earliest Muslims).”’
